title: Cybersecurity cold call example
intro: An IT leader already has a provider. Hear how the caller asks what the last security review covered.
takeaway: If the buyer names a gap in their incident response plan, find out who owns the next exercise before asking for a meeting.
sourceLabel: Read the full cybersecurity risk assessment script
relatedText: CallTeam’s manufacturing cybersecurity case study reports 9 qualified appointments in 90 days. Three advanced to sales opportunities.

turns.speaker: Caller
turns.line: When was the last time an independent team tested how you’d respond to a security incident?

turns.speaker: IT leader
turns.line: Our managed IT provider handles security.

turns.speaker: Caller
turns.line: What did their last review cover?

turns.speaker: IT leader
turns.line: They checked our tools. We haven’t tested our incident response plan.

turns.speaker: Caller
turns.line: Who would lead that exercise on your side?

turns.speaker: IT leader
turns.line: I’d lead it. Operations would need to be there.

turns.speaker: Caller
turns.line: Would 15 minutes Tuesday work to see what an independent review would cover?

turns.speaker: IT leader
turns.line: Ten Eastern works. I’ll bring our operations lead.

title: IT staffing cold call example
intro: A recruiter calls a hiring manager about an open network administrator job. The manager explains what the contractor has to do in the first week.
takeaway: Ask whether the employer can use an outside recruiter for the role. If the approved list is closed, record it and thank the buyer.
sourceLabel: Read the full IT staffing cold call script
relatedLabel: Read the staffing and recruiting outbound playbook

turns.speaker: Caller
turns.line: I saw your contract network administrator opening. Are you still hiring for it?

turns.speaker: Hiring manager
turns.line: Yes. We need someone who can run the cutover.

turns.speaker: Caller
turns.line: What would they need to handle on their own in the first week?

turns.speaker: Hiring manager
turns.line: The switch to the new network on Saturday night.

turns.speaker: Caller
turns.line: Can you bring in an outside recruiter for this role?

turns.speaker: Hiring manager
turns.line: No. Only approved agencies can submit, and the list is closed.

turns.speaker: Caller
turns.line: Got it. I’ll leave it there. Thanks for your time.

turns.speaker: Hiring manager
turns.line: Thanks for checking.

title: Appointment setting cold call example
intro: A parts supplier finds the item holding up orders and makes it the agenda for a short meeting.
takeawayHeading: Give the specialist enough to prepare
takeaway: Record the part, how many orders had to wait and the agreed meeting time. Tell the specialist the buyer will bring the part number.
sourceLabel: Read the full B2B appointment setting script
relatedLabel: Read what qualifies a B2B sales meeting

turns.speaker: Caller
turns.line: When a customer needs a part you don’t have, how do you find it today?

turns.speaker: Purchasing manager
turns.line: I call our two suppliers. If they’re out, the order sits.

turns.speaker: Caller
turns.line: Is there one part that keeps coming up?

turns.speaker: Purchasing manager
turns.line: A pump seal. We’ve had two orders wait for it this month.

turns.speaker: Caller
turns.line: Would ten minutes with our parts specialist help you check what would fit?

turns.speaker: Purchasing manager
turns.line: Yes. I can bring the part number.

turns.speaker: Caller
turns.line: Tuesday at ten Mountain or Wednesday at two Mountain?

turns.speaker: Purchasing manager
turns.line: Tuesday at ten. Let’s look at that seal.

title: Cold call voicemail example
intro: A caller offers a second repair estimate in a 20-second voicemail for a fleet manager.
takeaway: Give one reason to call back. Say the number slowly enough to write down. The clip uses an example number.
relatedLabel: See more B2B cold call voicemail scripts

turns.speaker: Caller
turns.line: Hi, Alex with CallTeam. I’m calling for a Calgary body shop that repairs service vans. If you ever need a second estimate, you can reach me at 403-555-0148. Again, that’s 403-555-0148.

title: “How did you get my number?” example
jumpLabel: How did you get my number?
intro: The buyer wants to know where the number came from. They ask the caller to take them off the list.
takeaway: Name the source you can verify, then pause. When someone asks you to stop, end the call and record the request before calling the next prospect.
sourceLabel: Read all four replies in the guide
relatedLabel: See when to use a mobile, direct or company number

turns.speaker: Buyer
turns.line: How did you get my number?

turns.speaker: Caller
turns.line: I found it in your company’s public staff directory.

turns.speaker: Buyer
turns.line: Thanks. Please take me off your list.

turns.speaker: Caller
turns.line: Understood. I’ll record your request and stop here.
